To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in a shallow lake with a low water volume, the diets of three sympatric zooplanctivorous fish species overlap, but when water volume increases the diets become less similar.

(1) trophic relationships among zooplanktivores are more complex in shallow than in normal conditions; (2) species segregation in shallow conditions is not based on the food resource; (3) the food niche breadth is a good index of species segregation; (4) trophic interactions are reduced when water volume recovers.

(1) the three sympatric species showed a significant difference in diet composition and niche breadth when comparing volume recovery and low volume conditions; (2) niche overlap was significantly reduced when the lake volume recovered; (3) species showed an intermediate to specialized feeding behavior, and (4) the potential for exploitative interaction increased during the critical low water volume.

the trophic interactions of zooplanktivores under volume change conditions in tropical shallow lakes, where the trophic segregation of sympatric species is reduced.
